name: Sunsama
summary: Daily planning that pulls tasks from your other tools into one deliberate schedule.
best_for: people whose problem is deciding what to do today rather than tracking what exists: it pulls from your existing tools and forces a daily plan, which is the whole product
skip_if: you already plan your day and just want a task list, because that is free everywhere; also skip it for a team, since there is no team pricing and the per-person cost multiplies straight through
honest_knock: There is no free plan after the 14-day trial and no cheaper tier: Pro at $22 a month billed monthly, or $17 billed yearly, per person, is the only self-serve option. Until at least 19 September 2026 the pricing page also contradicted itself (its FAQ said $25 and $20); by 19 November the FAQ matched the plan card. The other thing to be clear about is that this is per person with no team discount mentioned: two people is two subscriptions, and their own example says $44 a month.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month billed yearly ($204), $22 monthly, per person (plan card, FAQ and llms.txt agree on 19 Nov 2026)
pricing.notes: (re-read 19 and 23 November 2026 on sunsama.com/pricing and sunsama.com/llms.txt) Pro costs $22 a month per person billed monthly, or $17 a month billed yearly ($204 a year), with unlimited usage and integrations; Enterprise is quote-only. There is a 14-day free trial with no card required and no free plan after it. On 30 August and still on 19 September 2026 the FAQ on the same page said $25 a month per person, or $20 on yearly plans, which contradicted the plan card. On 19 November the FAQ gives the same $22 and $17 as the plan card and llms.txt, with a worked example of $44 a month for two people ($34 billed annually). The manifesto on the page still calls annual billing '20% off'; $17 against $22 is about 23% off, or $60 a year per person ($204 against $264). It also still explains that they price at $25.00 rather than $24.99 because they consider the latter 'deceitful psychological trickery', a figure no current plan uses.

measured.claim: My tasks sit in several tools and each morning I lose time deciding what to do first.
measured.observed: Half of this pain was tried. With no connection made, 10 tasks typed by hand and one prompt gave a day plan in about 1 minute and 45 seconds, of which the planning was about 25 seconds. Pulling tasks from several tools into one list was not tested, because every connection was skipped.
measured.plan: Trial account; 10 tasks were entered by hand and the planning agent made a day plan without any connection; the plans were read in the app and on the public pricing page; nothing was bought
measured.comparability: The pain of the audience group against a test with only hand typed tasks; no tool was connected.
measured.buying_consequence: The part about deciding what to do first got a plan in under two minutes; the part about tasks in several tools is open.

measured.claim: Plans are much better with your calendar and at least one task tool.
measured.observed: Setup complete said that no calendars and no task tools were connected and then led straight to the planning agent, which made a plan of 5 tasks. A plan with a calendar or a task tool was not made, so the difference was not seen.
measured.plan: Trial account; 10 tasks were entered by hand and the planning agent made a day plan without any connection; the plans were read in the app and on the public pricing page; nothing was bought
measured.comparability: The line of the setup screen against a test without any connection; no second plan was made to compare.
measured.buying_consequence: You can plan without connections, but the app itself says the result is better with them.

measured.claim: The planning agent deferred 6 tasks and adjusted 3 tasks.
measured.observed: After the prompt to focus on three tasks and keep to about four hours, the agent moved 6 tasks from Today to tomorrow, changed three tasks from Normal to Priority and showed Work: 4:05. The plan began at 19:00, after the end of the work day of 17:00 that was set in the setup, and ran to about 23:00.
measured.plan: Trial account; 10 tasks were entered by hand and the planning agent made a day plan without any connection; the plans were read in the app and on the public pricing page; nothing was bought
measured.comparability: The message of the agent against the day view; one prompt on one set of 10 tasks.
measured.buying_consequence: The agent does what the prompt asks and lands close to four hours, but it plans from the clock of the moment you ask.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session set up a trial of Sunsama with every calendar and tool connection skipped. Ten tasks were typed by hand and the app filled in the time estimates itself. A prompt to the planning agent (focus on three tasks, about four hours of work) gave a day plan: the agent deferred 6 tasks and adjusted 3 tasks and the day showed Work: 4:05. From the first task at 19:00:09 to the first day plan at about 19:01:50 took about 1 minute and 45 seconds, of which the planning itself was about 25 seconds. The plan started at 19:00, after the end of the work day of 17:00 set in the setup. Pulling in tasks from other tools was not tested. The trial lasts 14 days without a card, there is no free plan after it, and Pro costs $17 a month billed yearly ($204) or $22 a month billed monthly. The Continue button was not clicked, so no checkout was seen, and cancelling was not tried. Account and start: we created the account (a trial with 1 seat) and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser on 18 Nov 2026. The interface was already in English. The dossier name is Sunsama and the review is on OSM (osm/sunsama-review.html). Audience: the group Professionals with tasks spread over several tools; the pain is that tasks sit in several tools and each morning time is lost deciding what to do first. Setup: the setup began at step 1 (When do you work?, 9:00 to 17:00, Plan in the morning), then How do you structure your week? (left empty), Which calendars determine your availability? (Google, Outlook, iCloud and CalDAV; skipped with Next) and Where does your work live? (GitHub, Jira, Linear, Google Tasks, Asana, ClickUp, Todoist, Monday.com, Trello, Notion, Gmail, Microsoft 365 and Slack; skipped with Next). Setup went on without any connection. Setup complete said No calendars connected, No task tools connected and Plans are much better with your calendar and at least one task tool. Finish setup led straight to What would you like to do today? with the planning agent. Core action: 10 tasks were entered by hand with Add task or the key a, and the app filled in the time estimates itself (for example 2:00, 0:20, 0:45 and 1:00); it did not ask for them. Entering started at 19:00:09 and the first day plan (Review Plan) stood at about 19:01:50, so about 1 minute and 45 seconds in all; the planning itself took about 25 seconds (the screen says the planning usually takes 2-4 min). The prompt to the planning agent was: Focus on the report, the supplier call and the invoice batch. Keep it to about four hours of work. The result, word for word: The planning agent deferred 6 tasks and adjusted 3 tasks. Three tasks (Call supplier, Review invoice batch and Draft Q4 report) went from Normal to Priority, 6 tasks moved from Today to tomorrow and the day showed Work: 4:05, with a plan of 5 tasks. Next led to the Daily plan step (Planned for today, Obstacles in my way) and Get started to the day view for Wednesday November 18. The test ran at 19:00, after the end of the work day of 17:00 that was set in the setup; the plan started at 19:00 and ran to about 23:00. Several tools: pulling tasks in from other tools was not tested, because no calendar and no tool was connected and all tasks were typed in by hand. Plans up to the payment: Read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026. Public pricing page (sunsama.com/pricing): Pro Plan $17 per month, billed yearly (USD), and $22 per month, billed monthly; Enterprise on request (Contact Us); the page says Try it for free for 2 weeks., 14 day free trial and No credit card required. Unlimited access to all features. Inside the app (Settings, Billing): Sunsama Free Trial, 1 seat, 14 days remaining. The upgrade page says Your trial ends Thursday, Dec 3, and shows $17/mo billed $204 yearly (Save $60) or $22/mo billed monthly, with the button Continue with Sunsama Pro and the line Cancel anytime. The button was not clicked and no card field was seen, so no checkout total, tax or fee line was seen. FAQ on the upgrade page: Nothing is charged, we never asked for your card; when the trial ends you lose access to the workspace until you subscribe; there is no free plan after the trial. The dossier notes that the pricing page gives other amounts in its FAQ than on the plan card; that FAQ was not seen in this session, so only the plan card and the in-app page were compared with each other. Prices were not changed by this delivery. Cancelling: not tested; the FAQ says Workspace settings, Billing, Manage billing and cancel, access stays until the end of the current billing period and there are no refunds or prorated credits; there was no subscription to cancel. Not tested: all calendar and tool connections, the shutdown ritual, the weekly planning, the desktop and mobile apps, the AI briefing, the payment step and cancelling. Clean up (still so): the account, the 10 test tasks and the day plan stay; the timer on Call supplier was paused; the own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The day plan used the clock of the test: it started at 19:00 and ran to about 23:00, although the work day in the setup ended at 17:00. After the trial there is no free plan and access to the workspace is lost until you subscribe. The setup warns that plans are much better with a calendar and a task tool, so the plan seen here is the version without them.
